questions.question_text: Explain how the 'Right to Information' (RTI Act 2005) protects consumers in both commodity markets and public administration.
questions.correct_answer: In commodity markets, RTI ensures mandatory product label details (MRP, batch number, expiry date, ingredients). In public administration, RTI empowers citizens to demand official records on government service delays, tender details, and municipal works.
questions.explanation: Information access prevents seller fraud and ensures transparency in public service delivery.

questions.question_text: Outline the three-tier quasi-judicial redressal commission hierarchy established under COPRA and state their jurisdictional financial limits under 2019 rules.
questions.correct_answer: (1) District Consumer Commission: Original claims up to ₹1 crore. (2) State Consumer Commission: Original claims between ₹1 crore and ₹10 crore, plus appeals against District orders. (3) National Consumer Commission (New Delhi): Original claims exceeding ₹10 crore, plus appeals against State orders.
questions.explanation: The three-tier quasi-judicial structure provides stepped appeal channels culminating in the Supreme Court.
questions.hint_modal: Hint: Focus on the core definition of three-tier in chapter 5.

questions.question_text: Why is insisting on a formal cash receipt/bill at the time of purchase critical for enforcing the 'Right to Seek Redressal'?
questions.correct_answer: A cash receipt acts as mandatory legal documentary evidence of transaction before Consumer Commissions. Without a bill, dealers can deny selling the product, making it impossible to prove liability for defective goods or deficient service.
questions.explanation: Legal proof of purchase establishes seller-buyer privity of contract required by consumer courts.

questions.question_text: Case Study: Reji Mathew, a Class IX student, was paralyzed due to improper anesthesia administration during a routine surgery at a private clinic. Analyze which statutory consumer right was violated and trace the legal remedy pursued.
questions.correct_answer: Violation: Right to Safety (protection against life-threatening medical negligence). Legal remedy: His father filed a complaint in the State Consumer Commission and appealed to the National Consumer Commission, which found the clinic guilty of medical negligence and awarded ₹5 lakh compensation.
questions.explanation: Medical services fall under COPRA provisions; deficiency in medical care violates the Right to Safety, entitling victims to statutory compensation.
